y1: According to the law, a person with leprosy had to live outside the camp, crying out, “Unclean, unclean” {Lev. 13:45–46}. Anyone who touched him also became unclean.
y2: Jesus could have healed him with just a word, but He intentionally reached out His hand. The uncleanness did not transfer to Jesus; instead, Jesus' cleanness transferred to him.
y3: Jesus sent the healed man to the priest to offer the gift according to Moses' rule {Lev. 14}. This was the official way to return to society. Jesus restored not only his body but also his relationships.
y5: The centurion was an officer of the occupying Roman army, meaning he was a Gentile. He said, “I am also a man under authority. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes.” He understood that Jesus' word changes reality like a command.
y6: Jesus said, “I haven't found such great faith with anyone in Israel.” Many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham at the banquet in the kingdom of heaven.
y7: Although the Gospel of Matthew was written for Jews, Gentiles appear at the beginning (the wise men), the middle (the centurion, the Canaanite woman), and the end (all nations). The door to the banquet of God's Kingdom is open to all nations.
y9: When Peter's mother-in-law was healed from the fever, she got up and served Jesus. This same word is used in the scene where angels served Jesus {Matt. 4:11}. A healed person becomes a serving person.
y10: Matthew quotes Isaiah 53:4: “He took our weaknesses, and bore our diseases.” The prophecy about the Suffering Servant is first fulfilled in His healing ministry.
y11: In {Matt. 8:18–22}, Jesus says, “The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.” He lets those who saw the miracles know in advance that following Him is not an easy path.
y12: He Rebuked the Wind and the Sea
y13: The Sea of Galilee is 200 meters below sea level and surrounded by mountains, so violent winds suddenly arise. It was a storm so strong that even the disciples, who were fishermen, felt they were going to die.
y14: Jesus said, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” and rebuked the wind and the sea. In the Old Testament, only God calms the sea {Ps. 107:29}. The disciples' question, “What kind of man is this?” is the question of the entire Gospel of Matthew.
y15: Crossing the lake, Jesus heals two demon-possessed men in Gadara, a Gentile land {Matt. 8:28–34}. Both nature and evil spirits submit to Jesus' authority. But the townspeople cared more about losing their pigs and begged Jesus to leave.
verse: “The centurion answered, ‘Lord, I'm not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.’”
prayer: Jesus, I bow down to Your authority that commands sickness, distance, nature, and evil spirits. Touch me too with the hands that touched the marginalized. Let me believe in Your word like the centurion, and trust that You are with me even in the storm. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: leprosy. “Leprosy” in the Bible includes various skin diseases along with today's Hansen's disease. Religiously, it was considered “unclean” and isolated from society. Jesus was probably the first rabbi to touch a person with leprosy.
d1: cleanness. It is not a concept of hygiene, but the state of being able to participate in worship and community. “I want to. Be clean.”
d2: centurion. He commanded about 80–100 soldiers. He might have been from the army of Herod Antipas stationed in Capernaum. In the New Testament, centurions are usually portrayed positively {Matt. 27:54; Acts 10}.
d3: serve. The word “deacon” comes from this. Jesus also said, “I came to serve” {Matt. 20:28}. The first thing the healed mother-in-law did was serve.
